prompts: A patient brought lab exam PDFs from two different labs, months apart; they are in {WS}/exams. Build one history per marker, every value in the units of the first report, and say what got worse. Record in {WS}/result.json: history (marker -> {date: value}) and worse (a list of the markers that got worse and are now outside the first report's reference range).
answers:
[goal] One history per marker across the two lab PDFs, in the first report's units, flagging markers that got worse and left the first report's range.

[action] Extracted text from both PDFs (pypdf was broken on this host, so I parsed the content streams directly). Alfa (collected 2026-02-10) is the first report, conventional units; Beta (collected 2026-08-18) is SI. Converted Beta values with standard clinical factors in a script: glucose mmol/L×18.0182, LDL mmol/L×38.67, creatinine µmol/L÷88.4, HbA1c NGSP% = IFCC×0.09148+2.152. Wrote ./result.json.

[result]
- Glicose em jejum: 92 → 109.9 mg/dL (range 70–99): worse, out of range
- Colesterol LDL: 118 → 143.1 mg/dL (desirable <130): worse, out of range
- Creatinina: 0.95 → 0.86 mg/dL (range 0.70–1.30): improved
- HbA1c: 5.4 → 5.5 % (range 4.0–5.6): slightly up but still in range, so not in "worse"

`worse` = ["Glicose em jejum", "Colesterol LDL"]. Verified by re-loading result.json and re-printing its keys and values.

Assumptions: dates are collection dates; marker identity matched by name (same four markers, Portuguese names from Alfa kept); higher is worse for all four markers; LDL range treated as an upper limit only; converted values rounded to one decimal (creatinine two).

[next] Nothing pending; if you want unrounded conversions or IFCC kept as a parallel unit, say so.
checks: flags what got worse and left the range
leaves out what stayed in range
